questions.q: According to this lesson, what is "CI/CD" actually made of?
options: Three distinct practices — Continuous Integration, Continuous Delivery, and Continuous Deployment — chained together
A single tool that does everything automatically with no distinctions
Just Continuous Integration, with CD being a marketing term with no real meaning
A GitHub-exclusive feature not available on other platforms
questions.explain: CI/CD is a chain of three separate practices, each automating more of the release process than the one before it.

questions.q: What does Continuous Integration (CI) automate, specifically?
options: Automatically deploying every change straight to production
Automatically building and testing code on every push or pull request, catching breaks immediately
Manually reviewing code once per month
Writing commit messages automatically
questions.explain: CI's job is catching a broken build or failing test the moment a change is introduced, by running the build and test suite automatically on every push or PR.

questions.q: What is the one-word difference between Continuous Delivery and Continuous Deployment?
options: There is no real difference — they're interchangeable terms
Delivery makes every passing change release-ready but a human still approves the release; Deployment ships it automatically with no approval step
Delivery only works with Python; Deployment only works with JavaScript
Deployment is slower than Delivery by design
questions.explain: The practical difference is the final manual approval step: Delivery stops just short of shipping, Deployment removes that click entirely.

questions.q: According to this lesson, why might a bank processing regulated transactions prefer Continuous Delivery over Continuous Deployment?
options: Because banks are not allowed to use Git at all
Because Continuous Delivery keeps a releasable build always ready, while still letting release timing remain a deliberate business decision
Because Continuous Delivery is always faster than Deployment
Because regulated industries can't run automated tests
questions.explain: Continuous Delivery gives the always-ready benefit of CI/CD automation while keeping the actual release moment under deliberate human control.

questions.q: Per this lesson, is the CI/CD pattern specific to web application code?
options: Yes, it only applies to compiled binaries
Yes, it requires a dedicated mobile app
No — any 'build, verify, release' process benefits, including a dbt data pipeline running dbt run and dbt test before promoting models to production
No, but it only works with Python projects
questions.explain: The lesson explicitly notes that any build/verify/release-shaped process, including data pipelines, can use the same CI/CD mechanism — it isn't limited to application code.
